In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent. He who created death and life﴾. 'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: he means death in this world and life in the Hereafter.

Qatadah said: He meant the death and life of the human being in this world. Allah made the world a house of life and perishing, and made the Hereafter a house of recompense and permanence [See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/234].

It has been said that He mentioned death first because it is closer to subjugation (al-qahr). It was also said: He mentioned it first because it is older, since things at the beginning were in the state of death, like the sperm-drop and dust and similar things, and then life came upon them.

Ibn 'Abbas said: He created death in the form of a white-spotted (amlah) ram, which does not pass by anything, nor does anything smell its scent, without dying. And He created life in the form of a piebald mare (faras balqa') [female] [Omitted in "A"], which is the one that Jibril and the prophets used to ride. It does not pass by anything, nor does anything smell its scent, without coming to life. It is the one from whose hoofprint the Samiri took a handful and cast it upon the calf, and it came to life.

Fudayl ibn 'Iyad said: "Best in deed" means the most sincere and most correct of it. He said: A deed is not accepted until it is sincere and correct. Sincere means done for Allah; correct means done in accordance with the Sunnah.

Al-Hasan said: Which of you is most ascetic regarding this world and most abandoning of it.

Al-Farra' said: The testing has not been placed upon "ayyu" [except] [Omitted in "A"], and between them is an implied element, as you say: "I tested you so that I might see which of you is more obedient." A similar example is: "Ask them which of them will stand surety for that" [al-Qalam: 40], meaning: ask them and look which of them. So "ayyu" is in the nominative as the subject (mubtada'), and "ahsanu" is its predicate (khabar).

**Surah 67, verses 5–11**

﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven﴾. He means the lowest heaven nearest to the earth, which is the one people can see.

﴿with lamps﴾ [i.e., the stars, singular: *misbah*, which is a lamp, and the star was called a *misbah* because of its brightness] [[The text between the brackets is omitted in manuscript "A".]] for their light. ﴿And We made them missiles﴾, targets ﴿against the devils﴾ when they eavesdrop on the hearing. ﴿And We have prepared for them﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿the punishment of the Blaze﴾, the kindled Fire.

﴿For those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and what an evil destination.﴾ ﴿When they are cast into it, they will hear from it a roaring﴾, which is the first braying of a donkey, and that is the most hideous of sounds. ﴿And it boils up﴾ and seethes with them like the boiling of a cauldron. Mujahid said: it seethes with them as abundant water seethes with a little grain.

﴿It almost bursts with rage﴾, meaning it is nearly torn apart by its anger at them. Ibn Qutaybah said: it almost splits apart in rage against the disbelievers. ﴿Every time a group is cast into it﴾, a company of them, ﴿its keepers will ask them﴾ as a rebuke, ﴿Did no warner come to you?﴾, a messenger who would warn you.

﴿They will say: Yes, indeed a warner came to us, but we denied him and said: Allah has not sent down anything; you are only in great error.﴾ In manuscript "A" the word is *lil-rasul* (to the messenger) [[In "A": lil-rasul.]], in the singular.

﴿And they will say: If only we had listened﴾ to what the messengers brought us, ﴿or reasoned﴾ about it. Ibn Abbas said: If only we had listened to guidance or reasoned about it and acted upon it, ﴿we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: If only we had listened the way one listens who understands and reflects, or reasoned the way one reasons who distinguishes and considers, we would not have been among the people of the Fire.

﴿So they will confess their sin, and away with the companions of the Blaze!﴾ *Suhqan* means distance. Abu Ja'far and al-Kisa'i read *fasuhuqan* with a *dammah* on the *ha'* (*suhuqan*). The rest read it with a sukun on it (*suhqan*). The two are dialectal variants, like *ar-ru'ub* and *ar-ru'b* (fear), and *as-suht* and *as-suht* (unlawful gain).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 67, verse 12–16:

﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 67, verse 30:**

﴿Say: Have you considered: if your water should sink away into the earth, then who would bring you flowing water?﴾ *Ghā'iran* (sunk away), going down into the earth, so that neither hands nor buckets can reach it. Ata' said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: *ma'în* means *jari* (flowing).
